title: Finite affine refinement and Cartesian local model of a family descent datum
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], and fix a family descent datum $(V_i\to T_i,\phi_{ij})$ [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum]. Put $A=\coprod_iT_i$, $Z=\coprod_iV_i$ and let $D$ be a singleton descent datum on $Z\to A$ relative to $A\to T$ [def-pd-descent-datum] whose transport restricts to $\phi_{ij}$ on each component. Coproducts are those of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and all objects lie in the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For every affine open subscheme $U\subset T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], set $A_U=A\times_TU$ and $Z_U=Z\times_AA_U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a descent datum $D_U$ on $Z_U\to A_U$ relative to $A_U\to U$ such that projection $Z_U\to Z$ intertwines its transport with that of $D$ along $A_U\to A$ over $U\to T$. There exist $m\ge0$, indices $i(j)\in I$, and affine open subschemes $W_j\subset T_{i(j)}\times_TU$ whose images cover $U$, each flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] over $U$, with these additional properties. The coproduct $C=\coprod_{j=1}^m W_j$ is affine. Its induced morphism $p:C\to U$ is flat, surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], hence of finite presentation; $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The refinement induces $h:C\to A_U$ over $U$. The scheme $Z_U\times_{A_U}C$ admits a descent datum $E$ relative to $p$, whose projection to $Z_U$ is Cartesian over $h$ and intertwines the transports of $E$ and $D_U$. There is an isomorphism over $C$
$$Z_U\times_{A_U}C\cong\coprod_{j=1}^m Q_j,\qquad Q_j=V_{i(j)}\times_{T_{i(j)}}W_j,$$
where $W_j\to T_{i(j)}$ is the projection through $T_{i(j)}\times_TU$. This includes $U=\varnothing$ and $m=0$.

proof.text: Construct the transport on the specified pullback Z_U directly. Project a point x over r to Z, apply D.transport along r b and s b, and pair the transported point with s by the IsPullback universal property. The equality over T follows by postcomposing r a_U = s a_U with U to T and the Cartesian-square equation. The first projection gives the requested transport equation. The two projections reduce naturality, identity, and cocycle to the corresponding laws of D, giving the descent datum over U [def-pd-descent-datum], with the chosen fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. This direct construction works for arbitrary specified Cartesian squares, without a change-of-base assertion from the fixed-base pullback theorem.

source.place: Tag 023Y, lemma-pullback (1), construction along the square with bases U and T

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] to $U\to T$, giving the fppf family $B_i=T_i\times_TU\to U$ (interchanging the fibre-product projections if necessary). Apply [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] with the affine base $U$. It supplies finitely many indices $i(j)$ and affine opens $W_j\subset B_{i(j)}$, whose composites to $U$ are flat and locally of finite presentation and whose images cover $U$. This application uses the joint surjectivity clause of the fppf covering, not only the properties of its individual arrows.

Form $C=\coprod_jW_j$ and $p:C\to U$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. By clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], $C$ is affine. A point of $C$ belongs to one open component $W_j$, on which its local ring and the induced map from the local ring of $U$ are those for $W_j\to U$. Thus $p$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The affine neighbourhoods witnessing local finite presentation on $W_j$ are also affine open neighbourhoods in $C$, so [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] gives local finite presentation of $p$. The images of the components cover $U$, so $p$ is surjective. Since $C,U$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $p$ affine; clause (3) of the permanence lemma makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The finite-presentation assertion is now precisely the convention in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Tag 01I5, lemma-disjoint-union-affines; morphisms.tex Tags 01SH, lemma-morphism-affines-affine, and 01S7, lemma-affine-separated; Tag 01TP, definition-finite-presentation

proof.text: For every affine open $V\subset U$, affineness of $p$ means that $p^{-1}(V)$ is an affine open of $C$ by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Its image is exactly $V$, since $p$ is surjective. The singleton choice of this affine open, together with flatness already proved, meets [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Thus $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering; here we do not identify fpqc with a mere flat surjective family.

For each $j$, the map $W_j\to T_{i(j)}$ followed by the coprojection to $A$, together with $W_j\to U$, gives a unique $U$-map $h_j:W_j\to A_U$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The coproduct universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] assembles these maps into $h:C\to A_U$ with $a_Uh=p$. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-canonical-pullback-datum] to $a_U:A_U\to U$, $p:C\to U$, $h$, and $D_U$. Its conclusion gives $E$ on the chosen $Z_U\times_{A_U}C$ with the required transport equation. Its underlying projection square is Cartesian by the very definition of this fibre product.

source.place: Tag 023Y, lemma-pullback (1), applied with fixed base U

proof.text: Install the supplied colimit cofans as coproduct-existence instances and compare them with the chosen coproducts by their canonical colimit isomorphisms. The component equations hq identify q with the componentwise coproduct map. The component Cartesian-square clause of [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding] therefore gives IsPullback (inZ i) (V_i to T_i) q (inA i). Paste this square with each chosen pullback Q_j = V_i times_{T_i} W_j, then cancel the specified square Z_U to Z over A_U to A. The resulting squares exhibit Q_j as the pullback of Z_U along h_j. Finite coproducts of schemes are universal by [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] (Mathlib FinitaryPreExtensive.isUniversal_finiteCoproducts), so their coproduct is a pullback of Z_U along h. Comparison with the chosen pullback v h gives the isomorphism. The second projection equation of the pullback comparison is exactly the displayed equation over C. This uses only the component-square conclusion of the existing encoding theorem, not its construction or any assertion about the chosen singleton datum.

source.place: Tag 023X, lemma-family-is-one, component decompositions; Tag 023Y, lemma-pullback (1)

proof.text: All constructions and Mathlib instances above permit Fin 0. Neither the finite affine refinement theorem nor universality of finite coproducts requires a nonempty base or index type. Transport and comparison maps are defined by universal properties, so they require no point and no nonempty index type. Thus the same Lean proof handles the empty-base case, empty summands, and repeated selected indices without separate choices.
